subject: MSA + Order Form — publicity carveouts, logo use, evidence request
content:
--- Message 1/4: From: Elena Ruiz <elena@coredata.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-14 09:22 -0800
Subject: MSA / Order Form redlines — publicity & logo usage

Hi Lukas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Legal at CoreData attached a set of suggested redlines to the Order Form and the MSA related to publicity and reference rights. Two specific asks we want to confirm before we move to signature:

- Whether Redwood can confirm a limited publicity carveout for a joint press release and brief customer quote (one-sentence) tied to the Order Form signing date.
- Approval process and required assets for logo use (full color / one-color versions), and any embargo window your team expects.

We're attaching the redline doc and logo guidelines for your review. Our GC also asked for any evidence or attestations you can provide around confidentiality carveouts (e.g., who signs off internally, where approvals are stored) so their compliance team can close out.

Attachments: CoreData_Redlines.docx (docx), CoreData_Logo-Guidelines.pdf (pdf)

Can you confirm who on your side will be the final approver for publicity, and whether this is handled by Marketing (Marissa) or Legal (Lukas)? If you can give us an anticipated timeline (we're aiming to announce within 2 business weeks), that would be great.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Partnerships
CoreData Analytics

--- Message 2/4: From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@coredata.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-14 10:08 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form redlines — publicity & logo usage

Elena — thanks for the note and the redlines. Quick take from Legal below; Marissa / Ben will own the marketing and asset side.

- Publicity carveout: Redwood is okay with a one-sentence customer quote and a joint press release tied to the Order Form, provided the customer approves the final quote and release text prior to publication. We prefer a publisher approval loop rather than unilateral disclosures.
- Embargo: Redwood's standard practice is a 48–72 hour review/approvals window for product-related releases; for co-marketing/partner stories we can compress to 24 hours if Legal + Marketing confirm signoff. Please flag if CoreData needs a shorter window.
- Logo use: Marissa will review the attached guidelines and supply approved assets. Acceptable formats: SVG/PNG/eps; color and monochrome versions. No alterations other than resizing.
- Confidentiality carveouts: We don't keep separate attestations as a standalone file, but approvals are tracked in our contract record (HubSpot deal notes) and the final signed Order Form. If CoreData's GC requires a named approver, I (Lukas) will confirm in writing when signoff occurs.

Action items:
- Marissa: review CoreData_Logo-Guidelines.pdf and confirm permitted uses and any additional constraints.
- Ben: coordinate the Order Form redline session; propose acceptance or alternative language for the publicity clause.
- Elena: please send the preferred announcement window and any embargo constraints from CoreData.

Lukas Meyer
Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

--- Message 3/4: From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>; Elena Ruiz <elena@coredata.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-15 14:31 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form redlines — publicity & logo usage

Thanks, Lukas / Elena. Logged a few practical constraints from Marketing:

- Assets: we'll provide SVG and high-res PNGs. Please use the "Redwood Inference" wordmark only with the specified clearspace; do not pair with other logos in a way that implies a joint product unless both parties consent.
- Attribution: request that the quote attribution include job title and company only (e.g., "— Elena Ruiz, Head of Partnerships, CoreData Analytics"). We do not require any additional legalese in the byline.
- Embargo timing: 48 hours is fine for our team. If CoreData needs faster, we can look at 24 hours on a case-by-case basis.
- Co-brand placement: for press release and web mention, Redwood asks for placement parity (we expect Redwood to be credited at the same visual prominence as CoreData).

Small suggested language for the Order Form (suggested):
"Customer grants Redwood permission to issue a joint press release and use Customer's name and logo in marketing materials related to the Services, subject to Customer's prior written approval of the release and the quote."

If that looks good to CoreData, Ben — can you pull the suggested wording into the Order Form redline and confirm?

Marissa Cole
Head of Marketing
Redwood Inference

--- Message 4/4: From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@coredata.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-16 15:03 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form redlines — publicity & logo usage

Elena — looping back with the redline updates. I pulled Marissa's language into the Order Form and attached a single redline summary for quick review. Key points:

- We accepted the limited publicity carveout conditional on Customer approval of final text.
- Logo usage limited to supplied assets; no modifications.
- 48-hour review window standard; 24-hour exception by mutual agreement.

Next steps:
1) CoreData to confirm the announcement date (we have tentative week of Nov 29 if that works).
2) CoreData GC to confirm acceptance of the redline summary or propose a single counter-redline.
3) Once accepted, we'll attach the final executed Order Form to the HubSpot deal and Marissa will distribute approved logo assets.

For evidence: Lukas will post a signed confirmation into the contract record once Legal signs off. If your GC needs a signed internal memo or extra evidence, please specify and we'll handle it.

Attachments: CoreData_Redlines_Summary.docx (docx)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[End of thread]
